title: How Much You Need to Retire in a Low-Cost State (Florida, Texas, Tennessee)
description: Leveraging 0% income tax and cheaper housing to retire sooner.
content:
The 'Florida Retirement' isn't a cliche; it's a mathematical arbitrage. Moving from a high-tax, high-cost state to a state with no income tax and lower cost of living can instantly double the longevity of your portfolio. For retirees with a modest nest egg ($500k - $1M), Geo-Arbitrage is often the only way to stop working without dropping into poverty. This guide calculates the 'LCOL Discount' and highlights the hidden costs (Insurance, Property Tax) of popular low-cost destinations.

Key Takeaways

  • The Income Tax Bonus: States like FL, TX, TN, NV, WA, SD, and WY have 0% state income tax. This immediately increases your withdrawal purchasing power by 5-10%.
  • Housing Deflation: Selling a $800k home in the Northeast and buying a $400k home in the South unlocks $400k of equity for investment. This move alone can fund 10 years of retirement.
  • The Insurance Trap: While taxes are low, Homeowners Insurance in FL/TX is skyrocketing due to weather risk. Property Taxes in Texas are among the highest in the US. Do the 'Total Monthly Cost' math.
  • Lifestyle Inflation: LCOL areas often require more driving (higher gas/auto costs) and higher AC bills. Ensure your budget accounts for these shifts.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The 'Sun Belt' migration has raised prices in cities like Austin and Miami. True LCOL retirement now often means looking at Tier 2 cities (Knoxville, San Antonio, Jacksonville) rather than the hottest metros.

The LCOL Budget Model

Retiring on less than $1 Million is possible here.

The Budget

  • Housing: $1,500/mo (Mortgage/Tax/Ins on smaller home).
  • Living: $2,000/mo.
  • Health/Fun: $1,000/mo.
  • Total Spend: $54,000/year.

The Income Strategy

Social Security: $30,000/year.
Gap: $24,000/year needed from portfolio.

The Nest Egg

Using the 4% Rule: $24,000 / 0.04 = $600,000.
Verdict: You can retire comfortably with a portfolio that would be poverty-level in Boston.

Hidden Costs to Watch

  1. Property Tax Assessment: In Texas, they reassess property value annually. Your tax bill can jump 10% a year. Ensure your fixed income can handle variable taxes.
  2. Auto-Dependency: LCOL areas rarely have good transit. You will need 2 reliable cars for a couple. Budget for replacement cycles.
  3. Healthcare Access: Rural areas have cheaper housing but fewer hospitals. Ensure you are within 30 minutes of a major medical center for aging safety.
  4. The 'Heat' Tax: AC bills in Arizona/Florida run $300-$500/mo in summer. Level-pay billing helps smooth this out.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Florida still cheap?

North/Central Florida? Yes. Miami/Naples? No. Florida is two states financially. Avoid the coast to find value.

What is the 'Homestead Exemption'?

In FL and TX, declaring a home your primary residence shields a portion of its value from property taxes and caps annual assessment increases. File this immediately upon moving.

Does Tennessee tax dividends?

They used to (Hall Tax), but it was fully repealed in 2021. Tennessee is now fully tax-free on income and investments.
